title: Welcome, sister death
hookLine: nearly blind and ill, Francis adds a verse for sister death to his song of the creatures, and dies singing

cards: Near the end of his life, Francis's eyes are failing and his body is worn out. And in that state, tradition says, he makes a song.
It praises God for brother sun and sister moon, for brother wind and sister water, for brother fire, and for our sister, mother earth, who feeds us.
The words are in the everyday Italian of his hills, not church Latin, plain enough to sing. Later, the story goes, he adds lines for people who forgive and bear trouble in peace.
Then, when he learns he has little time left, he adds one more verse: praise for our sister, bodily death, whom no one living can escape.

teach.b: His early biographer, Thomas of Celano, tells it this way. A doctor tells Francis that death is near, and Francis answers with one word first: welcome. Welcome, my sister death.
Then he asks the brothers to sing his song to him, the new verse included.

Celano says he asked to be laid on the bare ground and began a psalm, the one that opens, in the King James Bible, "I cried unto the LORD with my voice." He died, the story says, with that psalm in the room. Why sister?

teach.h: EVERYTHING IN THE SONG IS FAMILY.
teach.b: Because in this song everything is family: the sun a brother, the water a sister, the earth a mother. Death isn't let in from outside. She belongs to the household of creation.
Francis isn't pretending death is pleasant; he is ill and in pain. He is naming it as kin.

teach.h: O DEATH, WHERE IS THY STING?
teach.b: Behind that is Paul's faith: "O death, where is thy sting?" For Paul, Christ's rising has taken the sting out. And the song is honest.
Right after the welcome, it warns those who die in grave sin and blesses those death finds doing God's will. Not every Christian speaks of death this gently.
Christians also keep a long practice of grief and lament, and John's Gospel says that on the way to the tomb of his friend Lazarus, "Jesus wept." Both live in one church.
Francis's word is one way of facing the end: open the door, use her name, and let the singing go on.

how: Franciscans and other Christians sing or pray Francis's Canticle of the Creatures, often called the Canticle of Brother Sun, and some read it at funerals or at the bedside of the dying.

games.q: you're Francis. a doctor has just told you death is near. what do you say?
o: ask the doctor to keep trying.
say welcome, my sister death, and ask for the song.
send everyone away and lie in silence.
games.why: by Celano's account he says welcome, my sister death, and asks the brothers to sing his song, the new verse included.

practice: If a loss is close right now, skip this and simply breathe; that is a full practice too. Otherwise, notice the breath going in and out, a gift that won't go on forever, and say two words quietly, sister death.
If you pray, borrow the psalm Francis began, I cried unto the LORD with my voice; if not, let the breath carry the minute.

wordCard.voice: Welcome. What Francis said, by Celano's account, when he heard death was near. He greeted her as a sister, not an enemy.

carryVoice: Your line: sister death. Not an enemy at the door, but family. See you tomorrow.
